points.text: No ablation of system components (reflection, HITL, modular teams, debug loop, tools)
No baseline agent: single-agent LLM or existing multi-agent code framework
Human-assisted and automatic results mixed without per-task disclosure; baselines lack human effort
Baseline implementation, hyperparameters and tuning budget unspecified
Specialized baselines mismatched or weak, e.g., FedNova for communication tasks
No variance or run counts; small margins within noise; reported generation unspecified
No validation split; evaluator and human see test accuracy, risking leakage
Global model evaluated on one client partition, mis-measuring non-IID accuracy
Benchmark task dataset/model specs inconsistent across tables
Identical specialized accuracies for Q7 and Q8 suggest transcription error
No token cost, wall-clock or success-rate reporting
Typos and symbol/caption inconsistencies
'Novel combinatorial strategy' for Q16 undescribed and unablated
Simulation round count differs between text and prompts
'Deployment-ready' claims unsupported by simulation-only evaluation
No privacy or security tasks in benchmark
No threat model for sending data to LLM APIs or executing generated code
Premise that algorithm selection is FL's main bottleneck unsupported
Templated fully-specified queries unrepresentative; ambiguous queries untested
Memorization vs synthesis not separated; benchmark-specific prompt scaffolding; no held-out tasks
No user study or human-effort measurement for lowering barrier claim
Related work omits ML-engineering agents, MLGym and FL automation
Planner-coder-tester pattern known; contribution incremental FL instantiation
No comparison with a generic ML-engineering agent
Cited 'single-agent' systems mischaracterized; premise unsupported
FL baselines not strongest standard methods (SCAFFOLD, MOON, local BN)
Q16 'novel' strategy is standard replay plus distillation; algorithm undescribed
Replay buffer vs exemplar-free TARGET is unequal resource setting
Citation errors (FedEWC, author naming, loose citations)
No comparison against simpler single agent
No ablation such as with vs without debug loop
'Competitive and often superior' overclaims; wins only 8 of 16
'Certified semantically correct' overclaims heuristic L2 checks
'Dramatically lowers barrier' and 'significant step' unevidenced
Generated strategies and failure cases not analysed
Results scattered over tables; losses not discussed; inconsistent conventions
Task definitions differ between tables
Typos in heading, caption and citation
No single-agent baseline
No leave-one-out ablation of multi-agent mechanism
Cited single-agent systems do not match characterization
'Competitive and often superior' contradicted by 8/16 losses
'Certified' claim exceeds 5-round smoke tests
Human intervention not marked per task; baselines got no human effort
Q16 gain uses replay vs exemplar-free baseline
Benchmark-specific scaffolding; developed on evaluation tasks; no held-out tasks
Unstated whether test accuracy influenced acceptance; no validation split
'Autonomous'/'deployment-ready' vs simulation-only human-assisted evaluation
Q2 and Q9 dataset specs differ across tables
Identical 63.62 for two datasets
FedEWC misattributed
No run count or variance
Reads as system design report; lacks ablations of design components
Human-in-the-loop makes experiments manipulable and comparison unfair
Architecture generic, nothing intrinsically federated-learning specific
No comparison against code-synthesis agent pipelines (SWE-Agent, CodeAct, etc.)
Similar agent frameworks not referenced; no new mechanism; novelty unjustified
Benchmark circular with system's template; no paraphrased or out-of-schema prompts
No confidence intervals, standard deviations or run counts
FL baselines measure learning accuracy, not synthesis performance; not comparable
No comparison to Copilot/Cursor given human verification needed
No ablations on prompt wording, agent count, LLM choice, planning vs coding
Heavy compute and simulation time limit scalability
Only 62.5% fully automatic; true autonomy not achieved
No comparison with other meta-agent systems
No standard deviations despite stochastic variability
No variances, confidence intervals, run counts or significance tests
Baseline fairness details scattered in appendix
Key configuration details not summarized in main text
Computational and LLM API costs not quantified

Human intervention confound; autonomy undisclosed per task
Specialized FL baselines weak or mismatched
Possible test leakage; no validation split
No threat model or code safety
Memorization and benchmark-specific scaffolding; no held-out tasks

Prior agent frameworks unreferenced; novelty unjustified
